91. Study the following statements :
(a) When she entered the drug store, Mrs. Higgins was not properly dressed.
(b) She looked like the mother of a guilty person.
(c) Mr. Carr did not expect her to be calm and dignified.
option_a: (a) and (b) are right but (c) is wrong.
option_b: (b) and (c) are right but (a) is wrong.
option_c: (a) and (c) are right but (b) is wrong.
option_d: (a) and (b) are wrong but (c) is right.

97. Which of the following statements is not correct ?
(1) Alfred was a petty thief.
(2) He stole cream, compact and lipstick from the store.
(3) At Mr. Carr's accusation, Alfred's mother felt intimidated.
(4) Yet, she was very gentle in responding to him.
option_b: He stole cream, compact and lipstick from the store.
option_c: At Mr. Carr's accusation, Alfred's mother felt intimidated.
option_d: Yet, she was very gentle in responding to him.

99. Which of the following statements is not correct ?
(1) At home, Mrs. Higgins would have been enraged.
(2) Outside, her conduct was like that of a caring mother.
(3) When she introduced herself, Mr. Carr felt stupefied
(4) He felt that he would have to forgive Alfred.
option_a: At home, Mrs. Higgins would have been enraged.
option_b: Outside, her conduct was like that of a caring mother.
option_c: When she introduced herself, Mr. Carr felt stupefied
option_d: He felt that he would have to forgive Alfred.

question_text:
100. A soldier is jealous about his honour as :
(1) he is jealous of his enemy.
(2) he is very sensitive about his honour.
(3) he is ferocious like a leopard.
(4) he wants to win at any cost.
option_a: he is jealous of his enemy.
option_b: he is very sensitive about his honour.
option_c: he is ferocious like a leopard.
option_d: he wants to win at any cost.

question_text:
101. '..... their exits and entrances.....'
The figure of speech used here is :
(1) Simile
(2) Metaphor
(3) Personification
(4) Hyperbole

102. A school-boy :
(1) is reluctant to go to school.
(2) looks beautiful in the morning.
(3) likes his teachers.
(4) both (1) and (2)
option_a: is reluctant to go to school.

question_text:
103. What do all men and women do ?
(1) perform various roles in life
(2) indulge in indoor games like chess, cards, etc.
(3) play outdoor games like football, cricket, etc.
(4) fight wars
option_b: indulge in indoor games like chess, cards, etc.
option_c: play outdoor games like football, cricket, etc.

question_text:
104. Why is the lover's sign compared to a furnace ?
(1) He gets angry very soon.
(2) He feels emotionally charged.
(3) He offers warmth to his beloved.
(4) He is writing a ballad.
option_c: He offers warmth to his beloved.

question_text:
105. Identify the figure of speech used in the first line.
(1) Simile
(2) Metaphor
(3) Personification
(4) Hyperbole

106. Which one of the following statements is NOT correct with respect to the given sentence ?
Sentence : Rhymes, songs and chants are ways for children to :
(1) extend vocabulary.
(2) memorize words and sentence structure.
(3) practise pronunciation.
(4) enhance expression and the rhythm of sentences.
option_d: enhance expression and the rhythm of sentences.

question_text:
107. Which one of the following is NOT true about using the library at the primary level ?
The library should not just be seen as a storage space for books, rather
(1) learners can be exposed to a variety of genres of children's literature.
(2) as an active environment for engagement with books.
(3) teachers and other adults can also model reading behaviour in the libraries.
(4) a read-aloud of the textbook can be best done in a library.
option_a: learners can be exposed to a variety of genres of children's literature.
option_b: as an active environment for engagement with books.
option_c: teachers and other adults can also model reading behaviour in the libraries.
option_d: a read-aloud of the textbook can be best done in a library.

question_text:
108. Which one of the following should be mastered to be literate ?
(1) Phonological awareness and fluency.
(2) Sight vocabulary and pattern recognition.
(3) Decoding and language comprehension.
(4) Accuracy and phonological comprehension.

109. Which one of the following is NOT correct about teaching grammar effectively ?
(1) Promote genuine communication.
(2) Elicit relevant rules of grammar.
(3) Provide practice in communication.
(4) Learn grammar by memorizing its rules.
option_d: Learn grammar by memorizing its rules.

question_text:
110. Literacy teaching approach that emphasise the relationship between letters and sounds is :
(1) whole language Approach
(2) grammar translation
(3) situational approach
(4) phonics instruction

111. A teacher in class III asked her learners to ask their partners five questions about their abilities using the word 'can', e.g can you swim ? This type of activity enhances :
(1) Oral fluency practice
(2) Controlled oral practice
(3) Free speaking
(4) Passive listening

112. A third-grade teacher wishes to establish a reading corner in her class. In making the judgements for selecting a children's book, which one of the following questions would be most important to be considered first ?
(1) Are the authors of these books well-known and respected authors of children's literature ?
(2) Are the books written for the independent reading level of most students in the class ?
(3) Will the books help address the goals of the third-grade reading curriculum ?
(4) Will these books be appropriate for use in more than one instructional context ?
option_a: Are the authors of these books well-known and respected authors of children's literature ?
option_b: Are the books written for the independent reading level of most students in the class ?
option_c: Will the books help address the goals of the third-grade reading curriculum ?
option_d: Will these books be appropriate for use in more than one instructional context ?

question_text:
113. Which approach/method is geared towards the learner's main goal of using language in a real-life context ?
(1) Natural approach
(2) Communicative approach
(3) Direct method
(4) Audio-lingual method

114. A teacher asked the learners to exchange workbooks and check their partners work. The objective of this task is to :
(1) give practice in extensive reading.
(2) give practice in using new vocabulary.
(3) give controlled practice of structures.
(4) develop the skill of peer correction.
option_b: give practice in using new vocabulary.
option_d: develop the skill of peer correction.

question_text:
115. Children in the foundational stage are more engaged in learning when :
(1) they sing rhymes after the teacher.
(2) they use multiple senses and actively use their hands.
(3) they trace or write letters repeatedly in their notebooks.
(4) they focus only on developing fine motor skills.
option_a: they sing rhymes after the teacher.
option_b: they use multiple senses and actively use their hands.
option_c: they trace or write letters repeatedly in their notebooks.
option_d: they focus only on developing fine motor skills.

question_text:
116. A student of class V says, "I give my work a final check for accuracy before submitting it to the teacher." The student is working at the writing stage of :
(1) Drafting
(2) Re-drafting
(3) Proof reading
(4) Peer-evaluation

117. Which approach/method doesn't encourage learners to use their native langauge in a language class ?
(1) Natural approach
(2) Communicative approach
(3) Direct method
(4) Audio-lingual method

118. A teacher is planning to collect a variety of Teaching Learning Materials (TLM) for his class II students. Which one of the following is NOT a correct criterion for choosing TLMs ?
(1) The material chosen should be attractive and safe for children of this age group to use.
(2) The material chosen should provide adequate opportunities for the children to explore and experiment with curiosity.
(3) The material chosen should be preferably locally made or locally available, as this would allow for easy replacement.
(4) The material chosen should be made by the children only and have some roughness to avoid slipperiness.
option_a: The material chosen should be attractive and safe for children of this age group to use.
option_b: The material chosen should provide adequate opportunities for the children to explore and experiment with curiosity.
option_c: The material chosen should be preferably locally made or locally available, as this would allow for easy replacement.
option_d: The material chosen should be made by the children only and have some roughness to avoid slipperiness.

question_text:
119. To create an inclusive, welcoming and joyful environment that supports every child's participation in achieving the competencies outlined in the National Curriculum Framework (NCF) can be best done by :
(1) conducting indoor activities and avoiding them from outdoor activities in scorching heat.
(2) majorly focusing on the learners good health and well being.
(3) displaying children's work from different domains of development.
(4) decorating the classroom for a colourful environment.
option_a: conducting indoor activities and avoiding them from outdoor activities in scorching heat.
option_b: majorly focusing on the learners good health and well being.
option_c: displaying children's work from different domains of development.
option_d: decorating the classroom for a colourful environment.
